rounds.text: Alpine Housing Development Corporation Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a steep discount to its intrinsic value of Rs 156 per share, which offers a robust margin of safety of 32.8% [E43, E44]. The company's underlying fundamentals demonstrate accelerating earnings momentum, highlighted by a 45% trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth and a 36% three-year profit growth [E20, E21], vastly outperforming the sector median profit growth of 2.0% [E62]. Furthermore, operational efficiency is surging, with the operating margin expanding by 9 percentage points over three years to reach 17% in the TTM [E30], backed by pristine cash generation including Rs 23.40 Cr in operating cash flow and an exceptional cash conversion ratio of 3.89x [E34, E35]. Balance sheet risk is remarkably low, evidenced by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.15x alongside decreasing total borrowings [E37, E38]. Conceded: the stock has suffered a 23% one-year price decline [E25] and the company currently pays a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], reflecting temporary market detachment from these rapidly improving fundamentals.

Fundamental returns remain underwhelming, demonstrated by a low 3-year median return on equity of 6% [E28] and an overall low ROE of 7% [E13] that triggered specific negative flags [E50, E59]. Operational efficiency is further undermined by exceptionally high debtors of 213 days [E52] and substantial contingent liabilities totaling Rs. 73.3 Cr [E51]. Recent market performance reflects this underlying disconnect, with compounded share price growth dropping -5% over 3 years [E24] and -23% over 1 year [E25]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong short-term profit growth and operating cash flow backing for the trailing period [E21, E34, E35].

While the bear highlights low ROE figures [E13, E28, E50, E59], the business outperforms sector medians with an ROE of 6.71% versus 4.3% [E9], an ROA of 4.27% versus 1.75% [E8], and an ROCE of 8.86% versus 5.57% [E10]. Furthermore, dismissing current sentiment ignores a powerful turnaround where results score 84/100 and trailing profit growth hits 45% [E21, E60].

Furthermore, the bull's dismissal of operational risks overlooks severe balance sheet red flags, specifically alarmingly high debtors of 213 days [E52] and substantial contingent liabilities of Rs. 73.3 Cr [E51].
